Hi Alex —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared definition of success and next steps. TL;DR: LedgerLane wants a pilot that proves accuracy for invoice parsing + an operational TCO estimate focused on token economics and batching/caching levers within a 3–6 week window.

What we heard (pain points)
- High per-document inference cost when processing long multi-page invoices (token-heavy).
- Intermittent spikes at month-end that make unit-cost unpredictable and cause long latencies.
- Security requirements: data residency for EU customers, audit log needs for procurement.

Goals (what success looks like)
1) Demonstrate 75–80% of current on-prem throughput at <=60% of their current per-document inference cost for the OCR+NLP pipeline.
2) Measure latency at 95th percentile under realistic bursting workloads.
3) Produce a short TCO with levers the team can act on: batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization tradeoffs.

Constraints you mentioned
- Annual inference budget capped near $220k for first-year production (approx).
- Procurement needs a sample SOW + security questionnaire answered to start contracting.
- Preferred pilot duration: 3–6 weeks; want a clear go/no-go within 6 weeks.

Proposed next steps
- I’ll share a 1-page pilot outline + token-econ playbook (attached) and a sample pilot config for your infra team to review.
- If procurement is aligned, we can target a pilot kickoff the week of Aug 24.
- Can we schedule a 30-min ops/infra sync with your SRE and our solutions engineer? I’m proposing Aug 18 or Aug 19 — which works?

Attachments: redwood-pilot-outline.pdf (one-pager), token-econ-playbook.xlsx (high-level unit economics)

Thanks again — happy to adjust based on procurement timeline.

Best,
Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Budget: the $220k is an internal stretch number; realistically procurement will prefer a pilot commitment < $75k unless the ROI numbers are very compelling.
- Spike handling: we need a clear fall-back if month-end bursts push latency beyond SLA — can you outline a throttling/fallback policy (e.g., degrade to a cheaper model or queue) and the expected impact on accuracy?
- Data residency: our EU traffic must stay in EU region; will that add material cost?

Procurement asked for two things before they’ll sign a simple SOW:
1) A short TCO example that shows per-document cost at three volumes (5k/mo, 50k/mo, 200k/mo) with and without batching/caching.
2) A copy of your SOC2 summary + answers to our standard security checklist (I attached the checklist to this reply).

We’re still interested in the 3–6 week pilot but price sensitivity is higher than I indicated on the call — can you prioritize a very tight, conservative economic example first?

Thanks,
Alex
VP Engineering | LedgerLane

Alex — great questions. I’m attaching a concise example TCO and a prioritized list of levers so procurement can see the conservative case up front. High-level answers below, then attachments.

1) Conservative TCO (summary)
- Assumptions: avg doc size = 1,800 tokens; baseline model = open-llm-v2 (standard fp16) but we show a quantized variant for cost comparisons.
- Per-document cost (conservative estimates)
  - 5k/mo: $0.42/doc (no batching) -> $0.27/doc (1s latency target with modest batching)
  - 50k/mo: $0.28/doc (no batching) -> $0.15/doc (with 8–16 batch & prefix caching)
  - 200k/mo: $0.18/doc (with large batching, caching, and quantized weights)

2) Spike/fallback policy
- Primary: autoscale dedicated pool with a capped burst to hosted spare capacity (explicit cost shown in attached model).
- Fallback options: model downgrade (higher latency, ~5–10% lower accuracy) or queueing + async processing for non-critical documents. We model both in the workbook.

3) EU data residency cost
- Serving in EU adds ~7–12% to unit cost in our model due to regional capacity premiums; included in the attached conservative rows.

Attachments: token-econ-playbook.xlsx (conservative TCO + sensitivity tabs), pilot-sample-config.json (sample pilot resource/config spec)

Proposed next steps
- I’ll ask Solutions Engineering to prepare a short config-focused runbook and a one-pager on tradeoffs.
- Can Procurement review the attached workbook and give us two budget scenarios they can accept (stretch vs conservative) by EOD Aug 17? That will let us scope pilot size.

If that timeline works I’ll schedule the infra sync for Aug 18 with our SE.

Best,
